3. Heard finally with the consent of the learned Counsel for the applicants, learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the non-applicant No.2.
4.

These applications are filed by the husband and relatives of the husband for quashing of the FIR in connection with Crime No.280/2023 registered with Police Station Morshi, District Amravati for the offence punishable under Sections 498- A, 354(A)(C), 504 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and the consequent proceeding arising out of the same bearing RCC No.425/2025 pending before the learned Judicial Magistrate First Class, Morshi.

5. The applicants in Criminal Application (APL) No.1129/2023 are the mother-in-law and the nearest relatives of the husband, whereas the Criminal Application (APL) No.1215/2023 is filed by the husband.

The crime is registered on the basis of a report lodged by the non-applicant No.2 on an allegation that her marriage was performed with the applicant Aakash s/o Bhaskar Mahurkar on 23.02.2023 at Morshi.
After marriage, she resumed cohabitation at the house of the present applicants.
All the applicants were residing jointly.

Applicant No.3 in Criminal Application (APL)
No.1129/2023 is her sister-in- 34..apl.1215.2023 and 1129.2023.Judgment.odt law.

It is alleged by her that her father has incurred the expenses of the said marriage when she resumed the cohabitation on the fourth day of marriage,
the applicant husband has obtained her obscene photographs and when she resisted the same, he abused and assaulted her by saying that being he is husband, he has every right to obtain the obscene photographs of her.
She has disclosed the said incident to her mother-in-law, but she has also ignored the same, and on the contrary, abused her.

It is further alleged that the husband has also suspected her character and on suspecting her character, used to abuse her and when she narrated the said incident to the other family members, they have also ignored the same.
She has specifically alleged that her parents were called for the meeting and during that meeting also she was abused.
It is alleged by her that all the applicants have assaulted her on 23.03.2023, and therefore, she constrained to leave the matrimonial house and taken the shelter at her parent's house.

On the basis of the said report, police have registered the crime against the present applicants.
6.
Heard learned counsel for the applicants, who submitted that on the basis of a general, vague and omnibus allegations, all the applicants are implicated in the alleged offence.
He submitted that the allegations regarding obtaining the obscene photographs are omnibus, vague and not 34..apl.1215.2023 and 1129.2023.Judgment.odt substantiated by any material.

He submitted that even father-in-law is restrained when he approached to the Police Station.
Thus, the conduct of the non-applicant No.2 requires to be taken into consideration.

He submitted that considering no specific instances are narrated as far as the role of the presents is concerned and there is no specific allegations against all the applicants and therefore, the applications deserve to be allowed.
7.

Per contra, learned APP for the State and learned counsel for the non-applicant No.2 /complainant strongly opposed the said contention and submitted that specific instances are narrated as far as the applicants are concerned regarding the ill-treatment.
The grievous allegations are levelled regarding obtaining the obscene photographs by the husband and when the incident was narrated the other family members, they have also ignored the same.
This fact itself is sufficient to show what type of mental torture was there to the non-applicant No.2.
In view of that, applications deserve to be rejected.

8. On hearing both sides and on perusal of the entire investigation papers, it reveals that after the marriage on the fourth day itself, the obscene photographs were obtained by the 34..apl.1215.2023 and 1129.2023.Judgment.odt applicant husband and when she has resisted, she was not only abused but she was also assaulted by the husband.

It further reveals from the investigation papers that when she disclosed the said incident to other family members they have also supported the act of the husband of the non-applicant No.2.
9.

The inclusion of Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code by way of an amendment was intended to curb cruelty inflicted on a woman by her husband and his family, ensuring swift intervention by the State.
However, it is apparent that there is increase in such type of the incidents.
An offence is punishable under Section 498A of the IPC when a husband or his relative subjects a woman to cruelty, which may result in imprisonment for a term extending up to three years and a fine.
The Explanation under Section 498A of the IPC defines "cruelty" for the purpose of Section 498A of the IPC to mean any of the acts mentioned in clauses (a) or (b).
The first limb of clause (a) of the explanation of Section 498A of the IPC, states that "cruelty" means any wilful conduct that is of such a nature as is likely to drive the woman to commit suicide.

The second limb of clause (a) of the Explanation of Section 498A of the IPC, states that cruelty means any wilful conduct which is of such a nature as to cause grave injury or danger to life, limb or health whether mental or physical.

The allegations is that the applicant's husband has obtained her obscene photographs and when she has narrated the said incident, instead of supporting her,
she was abused and humiliated in the house by other family members.

I am conscious about the fact that mere reference of the name of the relatives would not be sufficient to attract the offence punishable under Section 498A of IPC, but considering the allegations levelled that the act of the husband though disclosed by the non- applicant No.2, the other family members have not taken any action against the applicant husband, on the contrary, she was abused, assaulted and humiliated in the matrimonial house.

Thus, considering the nature of the allegations levelled against the present applicants, admittedly, there is a wilful conduct on the part of the present applicants, and therefore,
the applications deserve to be rejected.
